screen: Deck's own screen. Quick Access page window 854x454 css px (dpr 1.5) with the game running after the plugin reload.
setup: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor running (Context line names it), plugin reloaded after the launch, knowledge base on. Panel open on the Main tab with the ring on the question box (read focus), no question asked during any watch. As found: preset_chip_animation decode, preset_single_chip true. A page-side watcher read every slot of the chip row each 100 to 250 ms (label, whether the Tip badge is in the slot, whether the decode churn class is on, the slot's opacity) and logged each settled label change; the left stick was clicked (L3) once a minute during every watch. Settings were changed by an SSH edit of the one key and a plugin reload at once; each reload was followed by one failed and one good deck_openPlugin (as the runbook expects); each reload also restarted Steam's web helper for a few seconds (the game kept running).
pressed: L3 about once a minute during watches; the ring was walked to the question box before each watch.

watch_f_ring_hold_fade_one_chip.detail: Walked Up from the question box past the notes line, then back Down two stops to land on the chip (read focus: bonsai-preset-glass chip 'Any known Proton issues for this game?', a general chip, rect 48,291 300x30). Held 42.5 s reading every 250 ms. Chip text never changed; opacity stayed 1.00 the whole time; ring stayed on the chip. Then Down once: ring back on the question box (INPUT).

watch_b_fade_two_chips_7.2_min.note: In fade mode a chip fades out over about 1.4 s, is blank for about 0.5 s while its words swap, and fades in over about 1 s. So about every 4 to 8 seconds one chip is dim while the other is fully shown. In 46 of 430 one-second reads that dim one was the Tip chip, so the fully shown one was a general chip; in 3 reads the Tip chip was fully invisible. Two general chips were never on screen together. A first run of this watch (08:45) used the wrong filter (it ignored fading chips) and is not used.

seen.notes: The Tip stops in the walk read as 'Tip' because the badge's own label is 'Tip', so a Tip chip's accessible name is 'Tip', not its words. Tip chips were seen in the first 2 seconds of every watch (no 'no Tip chip at all' case). Shares: 0.53 to 0.55 everywhere. The share of Tip chips with decode, fade, static and carousel all sat inside one half to two thirds.

expected: a, c, d, e: never two general chips back to back, Tip chips between a half and two thirds of all shown (3-minute watches may miss the share); b: at every read at least one of the two is a Tip chip.
verdict: PASS: watch a (fade, one chip): no two general chips in a row, Tip share 0.54.
PASS: watch c (static, one chip, 3 minutes): no two general in a row, Tip share 0.53.

UNCLEAR: watch b (fade, two chips): two general chips were never shown together, but at 46 of 430 one-second reads the Tip chip was dimmed below half while the other chip was fully shown (3 reads fully invisible), so 'at every read at least one is a Tip chip' is true only if a dim chip counts. The owner decides what a read means.
